title: Base change towards spectra of fields
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(K)$ a scheme of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $S'$ be a $K$-scheme and $g:T\to S'$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of $K$-schemes. Set $X'=X\times_KS'$ and $Y=X'\times_{S'}T$, with projections $f':X'\to S'$, $h:Y\to X'$ and $e:Y\to T$. Thus both squares in
$$
\begin{array}{ccccc}
X&\longleftarrow&X'&\xleftarrow{\;h\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle f'}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle e}\\
\operatorname{Spec}(K)&\longleftarrow&S'&\xleftarrow{\;g\;}&T
\end{array}
$$
are cartesian. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on the small etale site $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] whose geometric stalks are torsion of orders invertible in $K$ [def-kun-torsion-invertible], the canonical exchange morphism of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], with abelian coefficients ($\Lambda=\mathbf Z$) and $F$ in degree zero,
$$
(f')^{-1}Rg_*F\longrightarrow Rh_*e^{-1}F
$$
is an isomorphism. This is the finite-type-over-$K$ case of Stacks Project, Tag 0F1I (etale-cohomology-lemma-punctual-base-change); no finite-type hypothesis on $S'$ or $T$ is imposed.

proof.text:
Work degree by degree. By [lem-kun-unbounded-exchange-agrees] the exchange at the sheaf $F[0]$ agrees with the bounded-below abelian exchange. By [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology], its degree-$q$ map is
$$\beta^q_F:(f')^{-1}R^qg_*F\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}F,$$
and in negative degrees both sides are zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], it is enough to prove that $\beta^q_F$ is an isomorphism for every $q\geq0$. In the remaining steps all higher direct images and all exchange maps are those of abelian sheaves; annihilation by $n$ is a property of such a sheaf, not a change of coefficient category.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, conclusion read on cohomology sheaves

proof.text: Reduce to bounded exponent, simultaneously for every $q$. By [lem-kun-invertible-orders-colimit], $F=\varinjlim_{n\in I_K}F[n]$, where $I_K$ is ordered by divisibility. This is filtered: $1\in I_K$ and $nm$ is an upper bound of $n,m\in I_K$. The sheaf $F[n]$ is annihilated by $n$. Inverse image is additive and exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], so $e^{-1}F[n]$ is also annihilated by $n$; its stalks are consequently torsion. The morphism $h$ is a base change of $g$, hence is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] to $g$ and $h$, and [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits] to $f'$ and $e$. They identify the source and target of $\beta^q_F$ with the colimits of the sources and targets of $\beta^q_{F[n]}$. Naturality in $F$ of the canonical exchange identifies its map with the colimit map. A colimit of a natural family of isomorphisms is an isomorphism: the inverse maps are natural and induce its inverse. Thus it remains to treat every abelian $F$ annihilated by a fixed positive integer $n$ invertible in $K$.

Choose an algebraic closure $\overline K$ of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Put bars on the four corners of the exchange square after base change to $\overline K$, and write $a:\overline{X'}\to X'$, $b:\overline{S'}\to S'$, $c:\overline T\to T$ and $d:\overline Y\to Y$ for the projections. The morphisms $g,h$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the preceding step, and $F,e^{-1}F$ are $n$-torsion; $n$ is invertible in both fields. Hence [lem-kun-0f1c], applied separately to $g$ and $h$, gives canonical isomorphisms
$$B_g:b^{-1}Rg_*F\xrightarrow{\sim}R\overline g_*c^{-1}F,\qquad B_h:a^{-1}Rh_*e^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}R\overline h_*d^{-1}e^{-1}F.$$
These comparisons respect the exchange map as follows. Let $E$ be the original derived exchange and $\overline E$ the exchange in the barred square at $c^{-1}F$. Under $a^{-1}(f')^{-1}=\overline{f'}^{-1}b^{-1}$ and $d^{-1}e^{-1}=\overline e^{-1}c^{-1}$, one has
$$B_h\circ a^{-1}E=\overline E\circ\overline{f'}^{-1}B_g.$$
Indeed, paste the inverse-image squares around this cube in either order. The two pasted inverse-image isomorphisms agree by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso-pasting]. Taking their mates, clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] gives exactly the two displayed composites. Thus an isomorphism $\overline E$ implies an isomorphism $a^{-1}E$. Moreover $\overline X$ is still finite type over $\overline K$: local finite type is preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], and quasi-compactness by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 0F1I, passage to the algebraic closure; Tag 0F1C for both direct images

proof.text: The functor $a^{-1}$ used in the preceding step is conservative on the objects in question. For every geometric point $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X'$, the induced field homomorphism $K\to\Omega$ extends to $\overline K\to\Omega$ by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed]. The pair consisting of $x$ and this field homomorphism defines a lift $\overline x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\overline{X'}$ by the fibre-product property. If $a^{-1}E$ is an isomorphism, then $x^{-1}E=\overline x^{-1}a^{-1}E$ is an isomorphism, using the composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. This holds for every $x$, so [lem-kun-stalk-faithful-derived] implies that $E$ is an isomorphism. We may therefore prove the assertion for algebraically closed $K$, retaining the fixed integer $n$ and the hypothesis $nF=0$.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, conservativity in the algebraic-closure reduction

proof.text: Now assume $K$ algebraically closed. Replace $X$ by $X_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism], $i:X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X$ is a universal homeomorphism and $X_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced. Its base changes $i':X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_KS'\to X'$ and $i_Y:X_{\mathrm{red}}\times_KT\to Y$ are universal homeomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-base-change]. By [thm-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-invariance], their inverse images are equivalences compatible with inverse image, direct image and cohomology. These equivalences identify $i'^{-1}(f')^{-1}Rg_*F$ with the reduced source and $i'^{-1}Rh_*e^{-1}F$ with the reduced target. They also identify the exchange arrows: the exchange is the adjoint mate of the inverse-image square followed by the counit [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], and transporting this adjunction through the stated equivalences preserves that square and counit. Thus the reduced exchange is an isomorphism if and only if the original one is. The reduction is still finite type over $K$: on a finite affine cover a finitely generated $K$-algebra is replaced by its quotient by the nilradical, which is generated by the images of the same generators. Henceforth $X$ is reduced and finite type over algebraically closed $K$.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, reduction of X and topological invariance

proof.text: Establish $BC(f,n,0)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, with the universal, cumulative meaning of [def-kun-bc-property]. The algebraically closed field $K$ is perfect: in positive characteristic every element has a $p$th root, and in characteristic zero fields are perfect. By [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect], $f$ is flat and of finite presentation, and $X_L$ is reduced for every extension $L/K$. For any $S'\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, the morphism $f':X\times_KS'\to S'$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and locally of finite presentation by clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Its geometric fibre at a point of $S'$ with algebraically closed residue extension $\Omega$ is $X_\Omega$, which is reduced by the same geometric-reducedness lemma. Thus [lem-kun-0eys] applies to every square formed from this $f'$ and any quasi-compact quasi-separated $g:T\to S'$, for every abelian sheaf annihilated by $n$. It gives an isomorphism in degree zero. By step 1 this is the degree-zero map in the definition of $BC(f,n,0)$; all negative degrees vanish. This proves that property for all base changes, not only for the particular $f'$ originally given.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, degree-zero base change after reduction; Tag 0EYS

proof.text:
Prove $BC(f,n,q)$ for all integers $q\geq0$ by induction. Step 6 is the base $q=0$. For $q\geq1$ assume $BC(f,n,q-1)$. If $BC(f,n,q)$ failed, [lem-kun-0f1d] would produce an affine integral normal $K$-scheme $S''$ with algebraically closed function field $L$, an integer $d\mid n$, and the projection
$$h'':X\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L\longrightarrow X\times_KS''$$
with $R^qh''_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}\ne0$. The hypotheses of that lemma hold: $f$ is a morphism of schemes, $q\geq1$, the preceding-degree property holds universally by the induction hypothesis, and $n$ is invertible on $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Apply [lem-kun-0f1i-normal] to this same finite-type $K$-scheme $X$, this $S''$, this $L$ and this divisor $d$. It gives $R^qh''_*\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}=0$, a contradiction. The equality of its projection with the one just displayed follows from $(X\times_KS'')\times_{S''}\operatorname{Spec}L=X\times_K\operatorname{Spec}L$. Therefore the induction step holds. By [def-kun-bc-property], every original square and every $F$ with $nF=0$ has isomorphic degree-$q$ exchange maps for all $q\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 0F1I, application of Tag 0F1D and the final normal-integral vanishing reduction

proof.text: Step 7 proves the bounded-exponent assertion in the reduced algebraically closed case. Step 5 returns it to arbitrary finite-type $X$ over that algebraically closed field, and steps 3 and 4 return it to the original field $K$. Step 2 then proves every degree-$q$ exchange is an isomorphism for the original torsion sheaf $F$. Negative degrees vanish and [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], with the map identification of step 1, implies that the stated canonical derived exchange is an isomorphism.
